meta.subtitle: How we score an unscored field on exposure and preparedness

blocks.kicker: I · THE CONSTRUCT BEHIND THE SCORE

blocks.text: Score an unscored population on a disciplined rubric, ship it clean and downloadable, and stay honest about what is measured versus assessed.

Britain is connecting data centres and grid-scale assets on terms that are increasingly not firm — interruptible, curtailable, or contingent on a connection queue that now runs to triple-digit gigawatts.{{cite:NESO-TEC,OFGEM-DEMAND-REFORM}} The financial consequence is breached SLAs and lost revenue, not physical damage. Nobody had published an outside-in map of who bears that exposure versus who can underwrite it. This page documents how we score {{fact:total}} market participants on Exposure versus Preparedness, fuse register readings with sourced research, and grade the index before anything is published as measurement.

Methodology is deliberately split from argument. Acts I–IV on the index page state the thesis: damage-first placement misses availability loss; two axes should separate posture; registers exist but the premium function ignores them. Findings is the empirical pass — four named predictions walked in order against the live slice. This page is the construct those predictions test: weights, λ, evidence tiers, pipeline loops. When registers refresh, ordering inside quadrants should move; the two-axis margin should not.

The competitive field already sells hazard modules, broker facilities, and parametric products, but none of those channels publishes a comparable outside-in map of non-firm posture across carriers, MGAs, brokers, assets and reinsurers. The architectural claim is that register-native measurement can precede the availability cover the market has not yet priced.

blocks.kicker: II · TWO AXES BEFORE ONE NUMBER

blocks.text: The same non-firm exposure is well-carried by an underwriter with data, products and capital — and dangerous in the hands of one without. A single hazard rank hides that split.

The thesis proposes that posture, not pedigree, should separate the field. Every entity carries two axis scores on 0–100 before any headline number: Exposure (the size of the non-firm bet) and Preparedness (the ability to carry it). Each axis is a weighted sum of five sub-factors rated 0–4, rescaled to 0–100. Scoring is arithmetic in code, never an LLM free-text opinion.

The axis score is E = (Σ wi · reff,i / 4) × 100 (and likewise P on the preparedness side): a weighted average of effective sub-factor ratings, where each reff fuses a register reading with a research reading (below). Margin of Safety = P − E is the surplus of preparedness over exposure. Findings prediction two tests whether posture, not pedigree, separates the tails on this margin. Quadrant cut-lines are in-sample medians on the live universe (currently exp ≥ {{fact:cut_exp}}, prep ≥ {{fact:cut_prep}}), not fixed 50/50, so the field re-centres as the universe grows.

blocks.kicker: III · HOW LARGE IS THE BET

blocks.text: How large is the bet? Exposure is judgement work dressed as a number: how much curtailable load sits in the book or asset base, how correlated that concentration is when a constraint event bites more than one insured at once, and how far damage-first wordings miss the loss.{{cite:ACT-HHI-EIOPA,PRA-PPP}} Reading registers and mapping boundaries is intelligence. Deciding how much of that tail to keep net is judgement.

Five sub-factors carry the score. Book concentration asks how much revenue or premium sits in classes where curtailment can bite. Non-firm intensity is the MW-weighted share on Gate 1 or flagged flexible connections when registers are live.{{cite:NESO-TEC,NGED-ECR}} Aggregation is Herfindahl concentration of covered MW across grid supply points and constraint boundaries — the sub-factor that turns benign singles into a correlated event. Trigger gap is whether filed wording can pay lawful switch-off at all.{{cite:ACAD-TEH-WOOLNOUGH-TRIGGER,ACAD-LICHTENBERG-TRIGGER}} Tenor mismatch captures multi-year policies against availability risk with almost no credible loss history.

blocks.kicker: IV · CAN THE FORM CARRY IT

blocks.text: Can this entity carry the risk it has written? Preparedness is not capital alone. It is whether the form, the data, and the pricing model treat curtailment as a first-class loss mechanism rather than a property-damage footnote.{{cite:LLOYDS-PARAMETRIC-CYBER,MGA-PARAMETRIX-SLA}} Product fit is the hinge: parametric availability triggers, SLA mirrors, and curtailment indices exist in fragments; most carrier wordings still wait for physical damage.

Underwriting expertise, telemetry, reinsurance depth, and pricing models must span power and interruption, not cat hazard footprints alone.{{cite:BROK-MARSH-NIMBUS,ACAD-BASIS-RISK-EXPECTILES}} In the competitive set, parametric MGAs and Lloyd's coverholders score highest on product fit: built for non-damage triggers. Composite carriers and wholesale brokers score on capital and market access but often carry a trigger gap on energy BI. Preparedness maps who can structure the cover, not who writes the largest premium today.

blocks.caption: The rubric encoded in software — sub-factor weights within each axis.

blocks.text: Outside-in research faces known half-knowns. Data points like gate status, segmental revenue, and pricing methodology can sometimes be measured from public sources — and sometimes cannot be found for every entity. The construct excludes what it cannot verify, and labels what remains.

Each sub-factor can carry two ratings: a deterministic rating from a register or filing, and a latent rating from sourced research. The effective rating is a credibility-weighted blend{{cite:ACT-CREDIBILITY}}: reff = clamp( λ·rdet + (1−λ)·rlat ), where λ is set by the evidence tier of the deterministic input. That fusion is the mechanism behind Findings' compounding loop: judgement on assessed inputs today becomes intelligence once register tiers land tomorrow.

blocks.text: Non-firm power risk lives across a value chain and a rulebook. We score four entity layers plus a fifth rules feed that re-prices firmness when regulation changes — the same in-force discipline as a live regulatory product. Exposure on Gate-1 connections runs ahead of any single carrier's preparedness score: two surfaces in the data, placement posture above and register facts below.

items.name: Carriers & syndicates
items.role: Hold the balance sheet. Exposure is energy / DC premium concentration; preparedness is capital, products, and curtailment pricing expertise.

items.name: MGAs & brokers
items.role: Price and place without mostly carrying the balance sheet. Exposure is risk routed through facilities; preparedness is products they can structure.

items.name: Energy & data-centre assets
items.role: Originate the exposure. Exposure is flexible-connection share and queue position from NESO TEC Gate column and DNO ECR flexible flags; preparedness is backup and monitoring.
items.examples: Hyperscale campuses, batteries on Gate-1 / curtailable connections

items.name: Reinsurers & capacity
items.role: Stand behind carriers. Exposure is correlated tail across cedants; preparedness is rated capital and correlation modelling.

items.name: Rules feed
items.role: In-force CUSC / Grid Code mods and NESO/Ofgem decisions. Defines what firm legally means; flags records for re-score.

blocks.caption: In-force rules that re-price firmness on the live index — the register moves; damage triangles lag.

blocks.text: The research methodology would have been impossible to run by hand at this scale. The move was to define a fuzzy but disciplined rubric, encode it in software, and run it in parallel — like giving Ben Graham a Bloomberg terminal. What perfects the data is a set of named loops, each with a trigger, an input, an output, and an exit criterion. Nothing synthetic enters the scored universe; sourced research fills qualitative gaps only.

Each loop is idempotent and gate-checked: ingestion diffs register snapshots before scoring runs; scoring recomputes median cuts and propagates L3 firmness to linked carriers; validation and adversary passes triage sourcing drift; the L5 publication gate blocks export until blended measured share clears threshold. The site you read is always the output of the latest successful pass — not a hand-edited snapshot.

blocks.kicker: VIII · WHAT WE WILL NOT CLAIM YET

blocks.text: A large positive margin on assessed inputs alone is a hypothesis, not a finding. PROVISIONAL is epistemic hygiene — not a footnote.

The slice stays PROVISIONAL until blended measured/disclosed share reaches 60% (L5). At {{fact:measured_pct}} on {{fact:total}} entities the direction of each score is defensible; magnitudes firm up as register tiers land. This reflects the live universe on each build, not a stale eval report. Per-entity drill-down shows each rating's provenance.

Argument evolution, stated plainly: ordering inside quadrants should move as Gate 2 records and filings land; the two-axis margin and the four Findings predictions should not. Three preparedness sub-factors (data & monitoring, underwriting expertise, pricing & modelling) rest on judgement by nature, so the measurable load sits mostly on the exposure axis where registers and filings carry the weight.

The index grades itself L0–L8 on every build. L5 is the publication gate; L6 checks axis weight sums; L8 is full reproducibility from records through to the static site. We hide unreliable-but-fun data rather than let readers jump to conclusions the evidence cannot support.

blocks.caption: Latest eval report — refreshed on each build.

blocks.text: Every sub-factor maps to a named primary source — a connection register, statutory filing, rating, or filed wording — with the exact field recorded in the harness. No value is a model guess dressed as a measurement. Britain's disclosure regime (Companies House, FCA register, NESO open data) makes outside-in scoring more tractable here than in markets where private companies publish almost nothing.
